def count_path_partitions(n, edges):
    """
    Count the ways to partition the vertices of a tree into vertex-disjoint paths.

    You are given a tree with n vertices labeled 0..n-1 (1 <= n <= 200) as a
    list of exactly n-1 undirected edges (a, b), 0 <= a, b < n. Edges may
    appear in any order and either orientation; the input is guaranteed to be
    a tree (connected, acyclic). Each edge is a tuple of two ints.

    A *path partition* is a partition of the vertex set into nonempty blocks
    such that each block induces a subgraph of the tree that is a simple path.
    A single vertex counts as a path of length 0. A block is a set of
    vertices, so the two traversal directions of a path are the same block,
    and two partitions are equal iff they consist of the same blocks.

    Return a list of exactly n integers where the element at 0-based index i
    is the number of path partitions with exactly i+1 blocks, taken modulo
    998244353. (Index n-1 is always 1: every vertex in its own block. Index 0
    is 1 if the whole tree is a path, else 0.)

    Note: enumerating set partitions is astronomically slow already around
    n = 30, and blocks that are connected but not paths must not be counted.

    >>> count_path_partitions(1, [])
    [1]
    >>> count_path_partitions(3, [(0, 1), (1, 2)])
    [1, 2, 1]
    >>> count_path_partitions(4, [(1, 0), (2, 0), (0, 3)])
    [0, 3, 3, 1]
